newsitem.title: FRANCE: UIC sees risk of H2 loss bigger than H1.
newsitem.headline: UIC sees risk of H2 loss bigger than H1.

text.p: UIC, the troubled property financing arm of state insurer GAN which is in the middle of a major restructuring, said on Wednesday its second-half loss risked being considerably bigger than in the first half.

The group, which confirmed it was proceeding with a capital increase of 805 million francs, also said it would look at the group's shareholder funds at the end of 1996 to decide whether further steps were needed to ensure respect of solvency ratios.
UIC said it had decided in October to commission an external audit on 1996 accounts by the same group that carried out a 1995 audit, which preceded a large balance sheet clean up.

"Given the additional provisions that could be required as a result of the current latest audit, the loss in the second half could be considerably bigger than in the first half," the UIC statement said.
"At the close of the 1996 accounts, shareholder funds will be reexamined so that action can be taken if necessary to ensure respect of solvency ratios," it added.
The group confirmed that its restructuring and major cost reduction plan would involve the drawing up of a staff cutting programme, but it gave no details. It employs about 560 staff.

UIC, hit when the bottom fell out of the property market at the start of the 1990s, was recapitalised by parent company GAN first in 1995 to the tune of 2.993 billion francs, a sum equivalent to UIC's net consolidated losses.

UIC chief executive Pierre de Lauzun said in September that "the second half should be along the lines of the first-half trend" and that further losses were expected. A source close to the company predicted a one billion franc year loss.
UIC, or Union Industrielle de Credit, had a net attributable loss of 758 million francs for the first half of this year after property provisions of 621 million francs.
Property provisions in 1995 were 1.07 billion francs and the net attributable loss for 1995 was 1.68 billion francs.

Parent company Groupe des assurances Nationales, which is a candidate for privatisation, announced in October it had made a first-half net consolidated loss of 965 million francs mainly because of its property exposure.
